title: Quarterly Runway Lattice — Hosted API Demand Lanes & Model Catalog Commitments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: produce a publishable quarterly runway lattice that maps Hosted API demand tiers (alpha/beta/stable) to model-catalog commitments, capacity hedges, and canary windows. Scope: define commitments for each traffic lane, set hedging thresholds (burst buffer and reserved capacity targets), specify allowed fallback model variants (quantized / cheaper variants), and produce the operational playbook for rolling changes. This ticket focuses on the product-side choreography: stakeholder sign-off criteria, OKR alignment, rollout calendar, and the gating rules that will be handed to Engineering and SRE for implementation.

Why now: usage patterns show more pronounced long-tail traffic and seasonal bursts. We need a structure that lets us commit to predictable SLOs for priority customers while keeping runway flexibility for model rotations and cost optimization.

Key decisions to land in this ticket: 1) adopt a three-lane service lattice (alpha, cadence, critical) instead of simple tiering to better express experiment windows; 2) commit to explicit capacity-watermarks by lane (e.g., reserve 60% of QTD committed capacity for critical lane); 3) use model-variant fallback policy that prefers quantized variants with an allowed 5–10% quality delta for non-critical lanes.

Trade-offs noted: committing capacity improves predictability for customers but increases fixed costs; larger hedges reduce risk of throttles but increase capital commitment. Using quantized fallbacks reduces cost but requires stronger eval gating to avoid customer regressions. The plan balances these by tying lane assignment to customer SLA and traffic percentile, and by making fallback rules configurable per deployment (hosted / dedicated / private).
acceptance_criteria: Published runway lattice diagram with lane definitions and watermarks (alpha/cadence/critical)
Stakeholder sign-off from GTM, SRE, and Legal (recorded in comments)
Canary scheduling matrix (calendar + rollback triggers) documented and linked to the rollout runbook
Model fallback policy defined and enumerated (fallback model IDs + allowed quality delta) and handed to Model Ops
Dashboard filters and OKR tags created in Console for tracking lane-level metrics (latency, cost per token, error rate)
